newsitem.title: FRANCE: French retail consolidation not over -Auchan boss.
newsitem.headline: French retail consolidation not over -Auchan boss.

text.p: The chairman of privately held Auchan, the hypermarkets group which took over retailer Docks de France in August, said in a newspaper interview that Carrefour's move to take a stake in Cora signals that the consolidation in the French retail industry is far from over.

"It's one more action that shows that the concentration in retailing isn't complete. In any case, we're not looking at just the acquisition of a minority stake," Auchan head Francis Cordelette told the newspaper La Tribune. Carrefour last week said it had acquired 33 percent of the holding company controlling the Cora retail group.

"We have taken note of the government's intention to no longer permit the expansion of hypermarkets space. From that moment, external growth was the only possible alternative," Cordelette said, referring to a restrictive retail law enacted earlier this year to protect smaller shops and city centres.

He said Auchan would reorganise its stores to create one division grouping the 36 Mammouth superstores of between 3,500 and 6,500 square metres and a second one combining 52 Auchan and 31 Mammouth hypermarkets. The Mammouth chain is part of Docks, acquired by Auchan in August after a hostile takeover battle.
